chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Maymun, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) arrived in the state of Mut'ah (combining Umrah and Hajj) - on the night of Arafah, so he performed Tawaf and discharged from his Umrah (Ihram), then visited some of his female slaves, then he renewed his Ihram for Hajj and departed.

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: Ahalla: To discharge from the state of Ihram for Umrah, allowing the pilgrim to wear normal clothes and engage in permissible acts.
key_terms.أَهَلَّ: Ahalla: To renew the intention and state of Ihram for Hajj.
key_terms.جَوَارِيهِ: His female slaves: Referring to the concubines or female servants, indicating that sexual relations were permissible after exiting Umrah Ihram but before entering Hajj Ihram.
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: Night of Arafah: The night preceding the Day of Arafah, a significant time for ritual actions.
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: Mut'ah: A type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, exits Ihram, and then performs Hajj in the same season.

ai.seo_question: How did the Imams perform the ritual of Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of Hajj al-Tamattu' by Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), specifically highlighting the transition from Umrah to Hajj on the night of Arafah. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Ihram for Hajj can be renewed after completing Umrah rites, a key distinction in Fiqh al-Ja'fari regarding the timing of the second Ihram. The narration serves as a primary evidence for the permissibility of performing the Hajr (exit from Ihram) and re-entering Ihram for Hajj on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah or the night preceding it.
